title: Black-Body Radiation
notes: **Black body:** an idealized object that absorbs all incident radiation and emits radiation with a spectrum that depends only on its temperature.
**Spectrum shape:** the radiation intensity versus wavelength curve has a single peak. The peak shifts to shorter wavelengths as temperature increases.
**Stefan-Boltzmann law:** total energy radiated per unit area per unit time is $E = \sigma T^4$, where $\sigma = 5.67 \times 10^{-8}\,\text{W/m}^2\cdot\text{K}^4$.
**Emissivity $e$:** real bodies emit less than a black body. $e$ ranges from 0 to 1. A perfect black body has $e = 1$.
**Kirchhoff's law:** at thermal equilibrium, a good absorber is also a good emitter at the same wavelength. This is why black surfaces get hotter in sunlight and cool faster at night.
